title: Distance Between Two Numbers
short: The distance from a to b is |a − b|.

blocks.html: The absolute value of a number is its distance from $0$. With subtraction you can find the distance between any two numbers.
The distance between $a$ and $b$ on a number line is $|a - b|$. Subtracting in either order works, because $|a - b| = |b - a|$.

$a - b$ tells how far you move to get from $b$ to $a$, and its sign tells the direction. A distance has no direction, so we drop the sign with the absolute value. When the numbers are on opposite sides of $0$, you can also add their distances from $0$.

blocks.name: numberline
blocks.cap: From $A = -4$ to $B = 7$ is one jump of 11: $|7 - (-4)| = 11$.

blocks.title: Opposite sides of zero
steps: Check: $-4$ is 4 from $0$ and $7$ is 7 from $0$, and $4 + 7 = 11$ ✓.

blocks.title: Both negative
steps: Both are on the same side of $0$, so do not add their distances from $0$: $12 - 3 = 9$ ✓.

blocks.title: Above and below sea level
blocks.q: A bird flies at 15 m above sea level and a fish swims at 6.5 m below ($-6.5$ m). How far apart are they?

blocks.html: Getting a negative distance, like $-4 - 7 = -11$, and stopping there. Distances are never negative: take the absolute value. Another slip is adding the distances from $0$ when both numbers are on the same side.
